previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for left flank pain lasting 15 days, with a history of chronic myeloid leukemia, chronic graft-versus-host disease, and prior anticoagulant use. Imaging revealed subacute fractures in the left ribs, likely due to a previous fall, which explained the pain. A new soft tissue nodule in the right breast was incidentally found on CT and recommended for mammographic follow-up. The patient also reported bilateral leg pain with ambulation, suggestive of claudication, prompting a recommendation for outpatient ankle-brachial index testing. Pain was managed with oxycodone and gabapentin, and prednisone was tapered to 30 mg daily. The patient remained stable, with no acute abdominal process, and was discharged home with follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with chronic GVH of the eyes, 
mouth, skin, and liver who is now almost 3 and a half years from 
her allogeneic transplant, who was admitted for further 
evaluation of headaches, abdominal pain, and leg pain.  
 
ACTIVE ISSUES:

# Abdominal pain/body aches. Resolved over course of stay, 
likely related to PUD. Had waxing and waning abdominal pain, 
increased over past several days with nausea and vomiting x 1 
prior to admission. She has known history of gastritis and 
gastric ulcer (EGD ___ and chronic rib fractures and is due 
for repeat endoscopy in ___.  GVHD considered but 
prior GI biopsies did not reveal any such abnormalities (skin in 
___ c/w GVHD). CT abdomen and pelvis without cause for her 
pain. Labs normal. Abdominal pain resolved by the time of 
discharge. Counseled to continue omeprazole and zantac.
 
# Headaches: Has chronic headaches at night for ___ years 
radiating from the back of her neck. In the days prior to 
admission, she endorsed increasing constant headache diffusely. 
Neuro exam revealed limited neck range of motion, neck and 
shoulder
muscle spasm, and small muscle atrophy and weakness, though MR 
___ ruled out myelopathy. CT head was without acute process. 
LP was considered but this change in her headache pain 
self-resolved and she felt much more comfortable, therefore this 
invasive procedure was deferred. Rapamycin level was noted to be 
elevated, so her dose was decreased. This may have been a 
contributing factor. Cyclobenzaprine was prescribed to help with 
muscle spasms as needed.

# Diabetes: A1c 7.5%. Likely steroid-induced or at least 
exacerbated by steroids. ___ consult recommended starting 10 
units NPH at breakfast in order to have insulin levels 
coinciding with her prednisone dose. She received insulin 
teaching before discharge and is scheduled to have ___ 
follow-up as an outpatient.  
 
CHRONIC ISSUES:

# CML: Remains in remission from her leukemia following her 
allogeneic transplant. Her counts are noted for normal platelet 
count with persistent anemia. Her counts have overall improved 
since stopping her INH. Further management as an outpatient. 
 
# GVHD, extensive, chronic. Ms. ___ has had exacerbation of 
her chronic GVHD with increased transaminases, abdominal and 
joint pain, and significant eye discomfort. Complicated course 
with multiple attempts at decreasing her steroid requirement to 
control her GVHD. She continues with eye pain which remains a 
chronic issue. She reports that she is not taking the steroid 
eye drops at this time due to concern over cataracts. She will 
be seen by ophtho for further management as well as oncology for 
her GVHD. Rapamycin level was decreased due to the elevated 
level and her headaches, will need to be followed-up. 

# DVT/PE. History of increased LMWH level and creatinine with 
twice per day dosing and was put on once per day dosing. 
Continued Lovenox in-house. ___ consider changing to warfarin if 
adequate monitoring of her INR can be maintained as an 
outpatient.

this time. She remainED on Acyclovir (at twice per day dosing as 
she is more compliant with this), Bactrim, and Fluconazole. She 
was restarted on INH in ___ for history of latent TB. However 
with drop in blood counts and increased liver enzymes, this is 
currently on hold and continued to be held in the hospital.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure to care for you during while you were 
hospitalized. As you recall, you were admitted to the hospital 
from the clinic after developing headache pain and abdominal 
pain. You underwent tests of your head and abdomen that did not 
show any dangerous causes of the pain.

Your headache is most likely due to muscular tightness and 
discomfort. This improved after taking some medications for 
pain. Please continue to wear the soft neck collar at night to 
help relieve your pain. You may also take the cyclobenzaprine 
medication if your pain gets bad to help relax your muscles. Do 
not drive while taking this medication.

Your abdominal pain also improved while you were here. It is 
most likely due to the ulcer in your stomach. Please continue to 
take the omeprazole and Zantac that you are already taking to 
help treat this pain.

Please start to take the insulin medication (NPH) that you 
received in the hospital. This is important to keep your sugars 
under control.
